claims.statement: The synthetic notebook identifies Mara Vale as the recorded surveyor.
The synthetic charter ceremony occurred at North Harbor on 1500-06-15.
Mara Vale arrived at Inland Workshop in approximately 1503.
A second synthetic notebook places Mara Vale's arrival at Inland Workshop in approximately 1504.
The North Harbor council administered the Fixture Basin from 1500 through 1508.
The fixture groups two source-bound regional marker intervals as stages of one analytical Process without asserting diffusion, direction or mechanism.
Exchange markers were recorded in the Fixture Basin region from 1498 through 1503.
Comparable exchange markers were recorded in the South Coast region from 1504 through 1510.
Mara Vale was present at North Harbor from 1499 through 1501.
Only the trajectory endpoints are recorded; the route between North Harbor and Inland Workshop is unknown.
Mara Vale was present at Inland Workshop from 1504 through 1508.
Traveler Sol was recorded at Inland Workshop during 1505.
Boundary version A is the primary fixture reconstruction for 1498 through 1503.
Expanded boundary version B is the primary fixture reconstruction for 1504 through 1510.
An alternative fixture reconstruction excludes the eastern inlet from the 1504 boundary.
The fixture defines the South Coast analytical region for the 1504–1510 marker observations.
The synthetic register records Mara Vale and Keeper Ren in the same meeting at Inland Workshop on 1504-03-01.
During 1504–1505, Keeper Ren's proposed phrase influenced the wording adopted in the North Harbor council protocol.
A distant synthetic observation was logged at Far Observatory on 1504-03-01.
The modeled presence intervals for Mara Vale and Traveler Sol overlap at Inland Workshop during 1505.

uncertainties.description: The two synthetic sources give different approximate arrival years.
uncertainties.effect: The UI must show 1503 and 1504 as alternatives and must not interpolate a day.

uncertainties.description: The route between documented endpoints is unknown.
uncertainties.effect: No path geometry may be drawn as a documented movement.

uncertainties.description: The primary and alternative 1504 boundary reconstructions disagree about the eastern inlet.
uncertainties.effect: Both geometries must remain selectable; neither may silently overwrite the other.

uncertainties.description: The sources document marker intervals in two regions but do not establish diffusion, direction or mechanism.
uncertainties.effect: The Process remains an analytical grouping and must not be rendered as a directional historical flow.

uncertainties.description: One source attributes the adopted phrase to Ren's proposal while another attributes it to prior guild rules.
uncertainties.effect: The influence Relation remains contested and both EvidenceLinks must stay visible.

uncertainties.description: The fixture is intentionally sparse and synthetic.
uncertainties.effect: Missing objects cannot be interpreted as historical absence.
